key_insight: Turbulence alters ice-crystal alignment and scattering, so assuming perfectly horizontal crystals can underestimate ice-water content.
engineering_relevance: Orientation-aware scattering models can reduce biases in polarimetric radar, lidar and submillimeter ice-cloud retrievals.
method: Model overdamped spheroid orientations with settling-induced torque, rotational diffusion and intermittent turbulence.
Couple orientation statistics to Rayleigh, Rayleigh–Gans, T-matrix and specular scattering.
Express turbulence effects through Legendre moments of the orientation distribution.
evidence_signal: For the single-size shapes studied, combining specific differential phase with differential reflectivity limits retrieval bias to 25%; exploratory EarthCARE lidar analysis finds a compatible signature most frequently near −11°C.
watch_item: The 25% bias bound can fail for size distributions spanning the alignment transition because the observables weight crystal sizes differently.
paper_title: Scattering by Small Ice Crystals in Turbulence: From Orientation Statistics to Retrieval Biases
